sanskrit: पुरोधसां च मुख्यं मां विद्धि पार्थ बृहस्पतिम् । सेनानीनामहं स्कन्दः सरसामस्मि सागरः ॥
hindiTranslation: हे पार्थ  पुरोहितोंमें मुख्य बृहस्पतिको मेरा स्वरूप समझो ।  सेनापतियोंमें स्कन्द और जलाशयोंमें समुद्र मैं हूँ ॥
englishTranslation: Among priests, know Me as Brihaspati; among commanders, I am Skanda; among waters, I am the ocean.
essence: Greatness in the world is a trace of Krishna everywhere.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Krishna says he is the highest among priests, the commander Skanda, and the ocean among all waters.
simpleInsight: The world is not separate from the divine presence you move through every day.
detailedMeaning: Krishna keeps describing how his presence shows up in the world around Arjuna. After naming the greatest among beings and powers, he points to Brihaspati, Skanda, and the ocean to show that excellence and vastness are reflections of him.
modernRelevance: On a family trip to the sea at Puri, you stand at the shore and feel small before the water. Krishna says that among waters he is the ocean, so the vastness you feel is a glimpse of him.
translationLiteral: पुरोधसाम् (among priests) / च (and) / मुख्यम् (the chief) / माम् (Me) / विद्धि (know) / पार्थ (O Partha) / बृहस्पतिम् (Brihaspati) / सेनानीनाम् (among commanders) / अहम् (I) / स्कन्दः (Skanda) / सरसाम् (among waters) / अस्मि (am) / सागरः (the ocean)
insight: Brihaspati among priests, Skanda among generals, the ocean among waters: excellence and vastness point to Krishna.
